id.meaning: Identifier of one published row, unique within one (acquisition, resource_id) and not across them. A hash of the source key, external_id and source_occurrence, so repeated source rows within a resource remain distinct. Neither the acquisition nor the resource goes into it, so rows of different resources or acquisitions with the same id are the same source record, captured more than once. To key rows across a whole table, use (acquisition, resource_id, id).
id.known_gaps: Not a table-wide key. On 2026-09-28 (spending-tables review N1) cihr.awards had 220,857 rows and 60,644 distinct ids: the three archive captures and the live resource carry the same id for the same award, so an id appears up to 4 times. 191,841 proactive_grants ids appear in both the live and the archive acquisition. The shared id is also how an archive copy of a live record is recognized (the registry counts `<source>@archive_import` evidence once). The asset check ids_unique_within_resource tests uniqueness within each (acquisition, resource_id).

external_id.meaning: The source's own identifier for the record, or a hash of the source fields that identify it when the source has no single identifier. The per-asset `external_id` note says which fields are used.
external_id.blank_means: Never blank. Records without an identifier are rejected, except explicit aggregate rows.

canonical_id.meaning: Groups revisions of the same underlying agreement or contract, such as amendments. Rows sharing a canonical_id are versions of one thing and must not be summed together.
canonical_id.blank_means: Never blank. Equals external_id when the source has no revision concept.

source_occurrence.meaning: 1-based count of how many times this record identity has appeared so far in the same source release. Values above 1 are exact or near duplicates published by the source. A row above 1 whose every other column equals an earlier row's is a content copy; entity creation and payers_resolved count it as that earlier row.
source_occurrence.known_gaps: Some sources repeat keys legitimately: on 2026-09-26 the share of rows above 1 was 53.9% in the NSERC archive import, 0.7% in SSHRC, 0.2% in NSERC live, 0.02% in transfer payments and 0 elsewhere. A snapshot whose share jumps is held before publication (spending.duplicate_guard, docs/RUNBOOK.md "Duplicate guard"), and a registry release fails the blocking check spending_duplicates_bounded when a slice's share of occurrences from such rows exceeds its usual share plus 5 points. The proactive contracts capture of 2026-09-27 04:59 UTC was published before the guard with every row twice (2,626,552 rows, Iceberg snapshot 799428121995713838). The table was rolled back to the 2026-09-26 snapshot (2534519102996296639, 1,313,276 rows) and the capture's publication withdrawn; since 2026-09-30 the rows are in PostgreSQL, backfilled from the held capture. On 2026-09-28 TBS still served the file doubled, so the guard keeps the table at the 2026-09-26 capture until TBS fixes it.

source_key.meaning: The Fact Factory adapter that collected the record.

acquisition.meaning: How the capture this row was parsed from arrived. `live` rows come from a collector's own fetch; `archive_import` rows come from an external archive imported later, which may be partial or overlap live data. Current source data is `acquisition = 'live'`.

resource_id.meaning: Identifies the source resource (one file or feed) the row came from. A hash of source_key and the CKAN resource ID, or of the configured URL when there is no CKAN ID; archive imports also hash the acquisition, so they never share a resource with live data. One resource of one acquisition is replaced as a unit on each update.

source_url.meaning: The URL the source release was downloaded from.

source_sha256.meaning: SHA-256 of the exact source bytes this row was parsed from. The bytes are retained in R2 under sha256/<first two characters>/<digest>.

parser_version.meaning: Version of the parsing rules that produced the row. A parser change publishes a new version and keeps the old one.

raw_json.meaning: The complete original source record, as JSON, before any interpretation.
raw_json.blank_means: The source record is XML; see raw_xml.

raw_xml.meaning: The complete original source record as XML.
raw_xml.blank_means: The source record is not XML.

extra_json.meaning: Additional attributes produced by the parser that have no typed column, such as historical capture status or archive member path and hash.

values.contract: A procurement contract or aggregated contract total.
values.transfer_payment: A transfer payment reported in the Public Accounts, or a proactive-disclosure agreement of type "O".

value_consistent.meaning: proactive_contracts only: whether contract_value equals original_value plus amendment_value as the source publishes them. A blank amendment_value is no amendment (0). A false value flags a row whose total disagrees with its parts, such as a mistyped value; amount stays contract_value either way. Since parser spending-iceberg-v5.
value_consistent.blank_means: Not a proactive contract; or contract_value or original_value is blank or not a number (older reports have no original_value); or the row was published before spending-iceberg-v5.
value_consistent.known_gaps: On 2026-09-28, of 1,313,276 contract rows, 884,847 were consistent, 126,906 inconsistent and 301,523 had a blank original_value or contract_value. The largest inconsistency is BancTec (CANADA), INC., reference_number C-2024-2025-Q2-02238 (owner_org pwgsc-tpsgc, procurement_id EN92951708): contract_value 20,027,319,127.56 against original_value 15,000,000.0 and amendment_value -100,000.0, reported to TBS Open Government.

is_aggregated.meaning: True when the row summarizes several recipients or transactions rather than describing one, for example contracts under $10,000, "payments under $100,000" or an NSERC or SSHRC "Batch report | Report en lots" row. Transfer-payment rows whose recipient withholds the name or gives a count of recipients ("Names withheld (10,931 recipients)", "Name withheld", "Recoveries (38 recipients)") are aggregates too.

text_columns.meaning: How every published text column (title, description, payer, recipient, recipients, research_org, recipient_business_number, recipient_type, recipient_city, recipient_postal_code, province, country, program, principal_investigator) is cleaned, for every source, since parser spending-iceberg-v5 (NSERC spending-iceberg-nserc-v6; spending.clean_record). raw_json and raw_xml keep what the source wrote, and ids are computed before cleaning, so they do not change. (1) HTML entities with their closing semicolon are decoded ("&", "é", "Ł"), including title-cased ones ("&Amp;"); an ampersand that starts no entity ("R&D", "Speaking &notes") stays. (2) The tags of common HTML elements are removed (a, abbr, b, body, br, div, em, font, h1-h6, head, html, i, li, ol, p, small, span, strong, sub, sup, u, ul; spending.MARKUP), br, p, div, li, body and headings as a space. Other angle brackets stay ("MONTREAL <<ASKLIPIOS>>", "<$10,000"). (3) A value that is only a placeholder, compared case-insensitively after trimming, is published as null (spending.PLACEHOLDER_VALUES).
text_columns.place_placeholders: "ZZ", the grants code for an unknown province or country, in province and country only. In country, "NA" is not a placeholder: it is Namibia's ISO code (24 grants rows), and stays.
text_columns.kept: "REDACTED" (any case) is not a placeholder: it says the source withheld a value, and stays.
text_columns.evidence: Every listed placeholder was seen in the published tables on 2026-09-28 (spending-tables review N5 and a read-only scan): contracts recipient_postal_code "NA" (57,042), title "NA"/"N/A"/"#N/A"/"NULL" (739), recipient "NULL" (187); grants recipient_business_number "0" (18,534), "-" (1,713), "N/A", "None", "Not applicable", "s/o"; grants title and program "0" (4,894 each); grants research_org "NULL", "-", "N/A", "Not Available"; grants recipient_city "N/A", "NA", ".", "NIL"; grants province "NA", "N/A", "ZZ"; research_org "|" (45); NSERC province "NA" (2,390) and "NULL" (314); NSERC recipient "Inconnu"; NSERC and CIHR titles "TBD"; SSHRC principal_investigator "n/a" (147), title "0" (144) and province "Unknown" (110); CIHR province and country "Unknown" (1,394 each) and archive recipient "N/A" (253).
text_columns.known_gaps: Mojibake is left as published, since the right characters cannot be recovered: 392 contract recipients and 38 grants recipients with "Ã" or "Â" ("VOLTS ÃNERGIES"), and NSERC province "Qu?bec" on 4,672 rows of NSERC_FY2004_Expenditures.csv, whose file has a literal "?". The asset check text_placeholders_and_encoding still counts them, and a few placeholders not listed here ("n.a.", "--", "?").

title.meaning: Short name of the contract, agreement, award or project, in English where the source provides both languages.

description.meaning: Longer description or summary, in English where the source provides both languages.

program.meaning: Name of the funding program the record belongs to.
program.blank_means: The source does not report a program.

payer.meaning: The English name of the government organization that made the commitment or payment. Where the source gives a bilingual "English | Français" title, the English part. Since parser spending-iceberg-v5 (NSERC spending-iceberg-nserc-v6); earlier snapshots hold the bilingual title (proactive contracts and grants), the owner_org code (aggregated contracts) or an abbreviation (NSERC, SSHRC, CIHR).
payer.known_gaps: A name, not a controlled identifier; use payer_code where it is filled. The owner_org title is the organization's current CKAN title, so older rows carry today's name. Transfer payments name the department in wording that varies by year ("Indian Affairs and Northern Development", "INDIAN AFFAIRS AND NORTHERN DEVELOPMENT", "Department of Indigenous Services").

payer_code.meaning: The open.canada.ca organization code (CKAN owner_org, such as dnd-mdn) of the payer, as the source writes it, the same code for the same organization in every table. Entity resolution attributes a code to a registry entity (ca.open.owner_org identifiers; catalog/owner-org-codes.json for retired codes, resolve.attribute_payer_code). owner_org is the organization that holds the record now, so after a reorganization past records carry the successor's code (docs/entity-registry-v2.md, "Payer codes"). Since parser spending-iceberg-v5.
payer_code.blank_means: The source carries no organization code (transfer payments), or the row was published before spending-iceberg-v5.

recipient.meaning: The organization or person receiving the money, as named by the source.
recipient.blank_means: The source does not name a single recipient, including aggregate rows labelled "Multiple recipients".
recipient.known_gaps: Names are as published and are not matched to entities.

recipients.meaning: All organizations the source lists as implementing the activity, as named by the source.
recipients.blank_means: The source has no multi-recipient list. Only global_affairs_projects populates it.

principal_investigator.meaning: The lead researcher named on a research award.
principal_investigator.blank_means: Not a research award, or an aggregate row.

research_org.meaning: The research institution named on the record, where it is a different party from the recipient, such as the university of a researcher paid directly.
research_org.blank_means: The source names no research institution.

recipient_business_number.meaning: The recipient's Canada Revenue Agency business number, as the source writes it. Either the 9-digit BN or the 15-character program account (9 digits, two letters, four digits), sometimes with spaces or a masked program account such as XX9999.
recipient_business_number.blank_means: The source gives no business number. Individuals and many organizations have none.
recipient_business_number.known_gaps: Not validated. Some values are malformed or fail the check digit.

recipient_type.meaning: The source's own code for the kind of recipient, unchanged. See each asset's note for the code list.
recipient_type.blank_means: The source gives no recipient type.

recipient_city.meaning: City of the recipient, as the source writes it.
recipient_city.blank_means: The source does not report it.
recipient_city.known_gaps: Not normalized. Spelling and language vary by source.

recipient_postal_code.meaning: Postal code of the recipient, as the source writes it, including case and spacing.
recipient_postal_code.blank_means: The source does not report it.
recipient_postal_code.known_gaps: Not validated. Some sources publish only the first three characters (the forward sortation area); see each asset's note.

recipient_refs.meaning: The IATI organization identifier (participating-org/@ref) of each implementing organization, at the same position as its name in `recipients`, as the source writes it. Identifiers follow org-id.guide, such as XM-DAC-41130 or CA-CRA_ACR-3119219814.
recipient_refs.blank_means: The column is blank when the source has no multi-recipient list. An element is null when that organization has no ref.
recipient_refs.known_gaps: Not validated. Some refs are malformed or carry surrounding spaces.

province.meaning: Province or territory of the recipient, as the source writes it.
province.blank_means: The source does not report it.
province.known_gaps: Not normalized to a code. Spelling and language vary by source.

country.meaning: Country of the recipient, as the source writes it.
country.blank_means: The source does not report it.
country.known_gaps: Not normalized to a code. transfer_payments defaults to "CA" when blank. Other sources leave it blank.

amount.meaning: The single monetary value that best represents the record. Which source field fills it differs by asset and is stated in each asset's `amount` note. It is not necessarily money paid.
amount.blank_means: No single value is available, for example when a project has commitments in several currencies.
amount.known_gaps: Some parsers count missing component values as 0. See per-asset notes.

currency.meaning: ISO 4217 currency code of `amount`. CAD for every source except global_affairs_projects, which reports the commitment currency.
currency.blank_means: No single currency, because amount is blank for a mixed-currency project.

commitments_json.meaning: Total commitments by currency, as a JSON object from ISO 4217 code to decimal string.

fiscal_year.meaning: Four-digit year identifying the Government of Canada fiscal year (April to March) the record belongs to.
fiscal_year.blank_means: The source gives no parseable year.
fiscal_year.known_gaps: Derived per source (see the per-asset notes). Proactive grants, proactive contracts, CIHR and GAC use the April-to-March convention, verified; transfer payments give the start year (verified). Aggregated contracts publish a calendar year here. NSERC and SSHRC take the first four-digit year of their fiscal-year label, not verified against source documentation.

date.meaning: The record's principal date, such as contract date or agreement start date, when the source gives it in ISO format.
date.blank_means: No date, or a date the parser could not read. See date_raw.

date_raw.meaning: The principal date exactly as the source wrote it.

revision_rank_json.meaning: Sort key for ordering revisions that share a canonical_id, as a JSON array. Higher sorts later.
revision_rank_json.blank_means: The source has no revision ordering.

row_id.meaning: Identifier of one version of one registry row. A new version gets a new row_id; the old version is kept.

content_sha256.meaning: Hash of the row's values other than its source pointer. Two versions with the same hash are the same content.

source.meaning: Where this version came from, as JSON. `origin` is roster or resolution; roster rows add source_key, capture_sha256, capture_url and row_number, the exact place in the retained capture.

recorded_at.meaning: When we first recorded this version, as a Unix timestamp. Not when it became true in the world.

revision_id.meaning: The registry revision that first wrote this version (docs/continuous-registry-design.md). Revisions 1 to 14 are the releases before the continuous registry, under the same numbers.

retired_revision_id.meaning: The registry revision in which this version stopped being current. The registry as of revision R is every version with revision_id <= R and (retired_revision_id blank or > R). For mention_occurrences this holds only for retained revisions (the head, the latest snapshot and held snapshots); see entities/mention_occurrences.

valid_from.meaning: When the row became true in the world, at the precision the source gives (a year or an ISO date).

valid_to.meaning: When the row stopped being true in the world, at the precision the source gives.
valid_to.blank_means: Still true, or the source gives no end. The two are not distinguished in v1.

entity_id.meaning: Build Canada's identifier for one party, a ULID minted once and never reused. Published references use gid://buildcanada/Entity/<entity_id>.
entity_id.blank_means: In an occurrence, the party is not linked; see reason.

anchor.meaning: The roster record an entity was first built from, as <roster>:<record key>; a charity uses its BN9, which all its program accounts share; a federal predecessor uses buildcanada/federal_predecessors:<key>; an Ontario agency or ministry uses ca-on/tbs/provincial_agencies:<crosswalk key> (ministries ministry-<key>), a school board its board number, a conservation authority its CA_ID; a curated Indigenous government buildcanada/indigenous_governments:<key>. A provincial record merged with the registered charity that is the same body (rule charity-merge-v1, since registry-build-v2) keeps the charity's anchor ca/cra/charities:<bn9>, and so the charity's entity_id; attributes.merged names the provincial anchor; its rule is the merge rule version that first produced the row version, since registry-build-v5 left out of the content hash so a new rule version alone does not re-version the entity. A municipality, Indigenous roster entity or (since registry-build-v4) ISC tribal council that absorbed the charity that is the same body (charity-merge-v2 and v3, since registry-build-v3) keeps its own anchor and ID. Used to keep the same entity_id across releases. Not an identifier to cite.

entity_class.meaning: What kind of party the entity is.
entity_class.known_gaps: person is reserved; v1 has no person entities.

subtype.meaning: The class's controlled subtype, such as ministerial_department, municipal_government, first_nation or registered_charity; federal_predecessor for a dissolved federal body from buildcanada/federal_predecessors; since v2 week 4 provincial_ministry, provincial_agency, school_board and conservation_authority (government_org), provincial_crown_corporation (government_enterprise, an Ontario agency its crosswalk entry records as a government business enterprise), health_authority (government_org, a Quebec public health and social services establishment), and for charities hospital (CRA category 0100, sub-category 0006, no "foundation" or "fondation" in a name), university (category 0010 and a name on NSERC's list of eligible universities) and teaching_institution (the rest of category 0010); other charities stay registered_charity. Since registry-build-v2 a charity catalog/nserc-charity-crosswalk.json matches to an NSERC university is university whatever its name or category (the NSERC name itself is a resolution match key only, not stored on the entity); a merged provincial record keeps its provincial subtype (school_board, conservation_authority, provincial_agency, health_authority); federal_organization_unit is a GC organization code the TBS inventory does not list (Service Canada, the Geological Survey of Canada, the Canadian War Museum; mostly units of an inventory department or Crown corporation, so class government_org says only that it is federal); other_federal_organization is the TBS inventory's institutional form "Other Organizations" (Federal Judges, Statistics Survey Operations, the Director of Soldier Settlement). See docs/entity-registry-v1.md, "Entity classes", and docs/entity-registry-v2.md, "Model changes".
subtype.blank_means: Not blank on a roster entity since registry-build-v2. Before it, a GC organization code missing from the TBS inventory.

name.meaning: The entity's name as its roster publishes it, unchanged.
name.known_gaps: ISC publishes some First Nation names with "?" in place of a character, such as "?Akisq'nuk First Nation". They are kept as published.

aliases.meaning: Other names the roster gives for the same entity, such as a legal title or abbreviation.
aliases.blank_means: Empty list when there are none.

jurisdiction.meaning: The jurisdiction the entity belongs to, as a lowercase ISO 3166-2 code such as ca or ca-on.
jurisdiction.blank_means: The roster gives no province or country, as for First Nations.

status.meaning: The roster's own status for the entity, such as active, dissolved, inactive, transferred or registered; every federal predecessor is dissolved. `not_in_roster` means the entity's roster no longer lists it; the entity and its ID are kept. `redirected` means another entity now carries its record (redirected_to names it). Since registry-build-v3 an ended entity may still have no valid_to when its roster gives no date, as for the municipal roster's dissolved and inactive municipalities (88 and 12 in release 10). Since registry-build-v2 a roster that calls an entity active but gives it an end (TBS inventory org 258, Oshawa Port Authority, end 2024) makes it `inactive`, since it cannot be active after it ended and the roster does not say how it ended; attributes.inventory_active_with_end keeps both published values. A GC organization code with a blank status_statut and no end date is `active`, with attributes.status_inferred saying so.

namespace.meaning: Who issued an external identifier and what kind it is, such as ca.cra.bn9, ca.isc.band_number, ca.open.owner_org, or ca.tbs.phoenix (the GC concordance's Phoenix pay-system code). Since v2 week 4 also ca-on.tbs.agency (a key of catalog/ontario-crosswalk.json, assigned by Build Canada because the agencies list has none; ministries are ministry-<key>), ca-on.edu.board_number (Ontario Ministry of Education board number, such as B28010) and ca-on.mecp.ca_id (the conservation authority's CA_ID in the MECP administrative-area layer, 1 to 36). Since v2 week 8 also ca-qc.meq.organisme_code (MEQ's six-digit organisme code, CD_ORGNS, such as 711000) and ca-qc.msss.etab_code (MSSS's eight-digit establishment permit number, ETAB_CODE). Since v2 week 7 also ca-ab.edu.authority_code (Alberta Education's four-digit authority code, zero-padded, such as 3030). Since v2 week 6 also gleif.lei (a Legal Entity Identifier from GLEIF, attached to a federal corporation entity whose corporation number is the LEI record's registeredAs under registration authority RA000072; its source is the GLEIF row). ca.ised.corporation_number is a Corporations Canada corporation number as its CSV writes it (no hyphen, no leading zeros), on a corporation entity resolution minted and, since registry-build-v3 on an Indigenous roster entity whose curated row cites it (Manitoba Métis Federation 15484090, Inuvialuit Regional Corporation 1854488, Nunavut Tunngavik Incorporated 2592959, Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami 466069), with the row's BN9 as ca.cra.bn9; since registry-build-v4 also on the 17 ISC tribal councils whose identified row cites the federal corporation of their name (Matawa First Nations Management 2317851, and others), with its BN9.

value.meaning: The external identifier exactly as its issuer writes it.

verified.meaning: 1 when the identifier comes from its issuer's own register, or is a catalog CSD code that passed rule csd-verify-v1 against SGC 2021 (namespace ca.statcan.csd_uid); 0 when it is a crosswalk candidate that is unchecked or failed the check (namespace ca.statcan.csd_uid.unverified).

vintage.meaning: The edition of the code list the identifier belongs to, such as a census year.
vintage.blank_means: The code list is not versioned, or the vintage is not yet known.

subject_id.meaning: The entity the relationship is about.

predicate.meaning: The kind of relationship. One (subject_id, predicate, object_id, object_ref) holds one relationship; a build that produces two different ones on the same key fails.
predicate.known_gaps: administrative_part_of has no source loaded yet. succeeded_by comes only from the curated roster buildcanada/federal_predecessors (federal bodies dissolved before 2012 or not in the TBS inventory); municipal and later federal lineage is not loaded yet. A succeeded_by row's attributes carry event (renamed, reclassified, amalgamated, split, absorbed, transferred_functions), effective_date (the day the cited instrument came into force, not its assent) and, for renamed and absorbed only, boundary_rule successor, which resolution uses to give a straddling fiscal year to the successor; plus authority, locator, citation_sha256 and citations (see attributes). succeeded_by is lineage, not payment attribution; a predecessor's payments stay on the predecessor, and after a split nothing is allocated to either successor. covers (rule csd-cover-v1) links a county municipality made of several census subdivisions to each member CSD's DGUID (object_ref ca.statcan.dguid:<DGUID>), with attributes dguid, vintage, role member_csd and evidence (roster_csd_uids, census_division, sgc_capture_sha256); the county has no ca.statcan.csd_uid of its own and no DGUID located_within link. Only the nine Nova Scotia county municipalities qualify in the 2026-09-25 catalog (28 links). party_to links an Indigenous government, an ISC First Nation or an ISC tribal council to an agreement it signed (object_ref buildcanada.agreement:<key>, a key of catalog/indigenous-governments.json; agreements are not entities), with attributes role (signatory), effective_date (the year, month or day CIRNAC gives), agreement (its name) and the curated row's authority, locator, citation_sha256 and citations. It comes only from buildcanada/indigenous_governments. member_of links an ISC First Nation to its ISC tribal council (ca/isc/first_nation_tribal_councils, no attributes) or, from buildcanada/indigenous_governments, to the regional Indigenous government it is a member of (the Nisga'a villages, the Cree First Nations, and the four Tlicho bands, which the Tlicho Agreement says ceased in 2005 but ISC still lists), with the curated row's authority, locator, citation_sha256 and citations.

object_id.meaning: The entity on the other side of the relationship.
object_id.blank_means: The object is not an entity; see object_ref.

object_ref.meaning: A non-entity object, as <namespace>:<value>, such as ca.isc.reserve_number:07427 for land a First Nation governs or ca.statcan.dguid:2021A00054806011 for the 2021 census subdivision a municipality is located within.
object_ref.blank_means: The object is an entity; see object_id.

attributes.meaning: Predicate-specific values as JSON, such as percent, direct, holding_type, notes and locator for owned_by, or dguid and vintage for a located_within link to a census subdivision. A succeeded_by row carries authority (the instrument and its coming-into-force), locator (the first cited page's URL), citation_sha256 (that page's SHA-256 in content-addressed storage, captured unchanged) and citations (every cited page as locator, sha256 and pinpoint).
attributes.blank_means: Empty object when there are none.

occurrence_id.meaning: One party on one spending row, a hash of the source table, row id, field and array position. Stable across releases.

field.meaning: Which party field of the spending row the occurrence came from.

raw_name.meaning: The party's name exactly as the spending row publishes it.
raw_name.blank_means: The row gives no name; party_kind is unknown. A name with nothing to normalize (a lone bilingual separator "|", punctuation) is kept as published, with party_kind unknown and kind_reason blank_name (since occurrences-v5).

normalized_name.meaning: raw_name after the versioned normalization in entities/names.py (accents and punctuation removed, casefolded, legal-form suffixes dropped). Used only for exact matching.
normalized_name.blank_means: raw_name is blank or has nothing left after normalization.

party_kind.meaning: Whether the party is an organization, an individual, an aggregate of many recipients, or unknown.

method.meaning: The rule that linked the occurrence, or, when reason is proposed, the rule that proposed a link it is not yet active to make. ai_review when the effective decision is an AI review decision (reason blank, proposed or ai_undecided); correction when it is a human correction.

reason.meaning: Why an occurrence is not linked.
reason.known_gaps: conflict covers an identifier held by several entities and an identifier that disagrees with the name, except that since resolution-v4 a BN held only by federal corporations names the one Active corporation among them (else the one whose name is the row's), so an amalgamation's Inactive predecessors sharing the BN are not a conflict; since resolution-v5 a name matched only by federal corporations, one Active and every other Inactive - Amalgamated on its BN, is the Active one's for rows from its anniversary date on, and otherwise ambiguous; a payer's owner_org names the organization reporting the row (the open.canada.ca organization that holds it), so since resolution-v4 a row dated before that organization's validity is attributed to the cited predecessor (succeeded_by) its period falls in, else to the reporting organization itself (method payer_code, never period_spans_change for that organization's start), and retired codes no roster carries are named through catalog/owner-org-codes.json; rows after an organization ended keep interval matching; period_spans_change means the row's period (its row date, else its fiscal year April 1 to March 31) straddles a validity bound of the entity that would have been linked, at the bound's own precision (a year-only bound covers the whole year); a candidate whose validity the period lies wholly outside is not a candidate; a straddling fiscal year goes to the successor, not period_spans_change, when a renamed or absorbed succeeded_by row carries boundary_rule successor; since resolution-v6 an identifier whose holder is the row's body with a sibling qualifier (the row names X and the BN is X Foundation's, X Trust Fund's, X Investments' or X Public Library Board's, or the row names X Foundation, Trust Fund or Investments and the BN is X's) is a conflict, and national_name links a row with no province to the one entity (of the name+province rules) or federal corporation holding its exact name in any province; proposed means the rule in method matched one entity but is not active for this rule_version (catalog/entity-rule-activations.json), so the proposed entity is the first of candidates; rule_retired means the rule in method matched but its (method, versions) pair was retired (fact-factory entities retire-rule), kept like a proposal with the entity it would have linked first, or an AI review decision on the occurrence was retired with its pair and nothing else links it; ai_undecided means the effective AI review decision is not_same_as or cannot_decide, and the candidates are kept; corrected_unlinked means a human correction names no entity.

candidates.meaning: The entity IDs, or ca/ised/federal_corporations:<number> anchors for corporations not yet entities, that the rules found for an unlinked occurrence. For reason proposed, the proposed entity comes first.
candidates.blank_means: No candidates, or the occurrence is linked.

rule_version.meaning: The resolution, extraction, name-normalization and matching-eligibility (catalog/entity-matching.json) versions in force when this row version was written, joined by +. Rows before matching-v1 have three parts. resolution-v4 includes the owner_org codes table (catalog/owner-org-codes.json), whose digest it pins. Since incremental resolution (evidence-v1) it is not part of the row's content, so a release built under new versions keeps every row whose outcome is unchanged, with the versions it was first written under; the versions a release resolved under, which every occurrence as of that release stands for, are in its registry_releases.versions (resolve.release_versions). Before, every row was rewritten when a version changed, so the two agree for earlier releases.

decision_id.meaning: Identifier of one resolution decision, a hash of its content and the release that made it. Published references use gid://buildcanada/EntityResolutionDecision/<decision_id>.

subject.meaning: What the decision is about, an occurrence_id or, for entity-level decisions, an entity_id; subject_kind says which.

subject_kind.meaning: Whether subject is an occurrence or an entity.

outcome.meaning: What was decided about the subject.

entity_ref.meaning: A roster-reference candidate the decision names when it is not yet an entity, as JSON with ref, source_key, record_key, capture_id and row_sha256, the exact roster row the decider saw.
entity_ref.blank_means: The decision names an entity (entity_id), or none.

versions.meaning: What made the decision, as JSON. For a rule or model, the (method, versions) pair as one object, such as {"method": "exact_name", "resolution": ..., "extraction": ..., "normalization": ..., "matching": ...}; an ai_review pair adds prompt, model, candidate_generator and, for every reviewer but claude-opus-5, reasoning_effort (such as {"model": "openai/gpt-6-luna", "reasoning_effort": "xhigh"}), so each reviewer's decisions name their own pair; for a person, the reviewer and the correction file's digest.

input_sha256.meaning: Digest of the evidence the decider was shown (for AI review, the review unit key). A decision is reused only while the occurrence's current evidence gives the same digest.
input_sha256.blank_means: The decision is not bound to a digest, as for a rule's own outcome.

evidence.meaning: What the decider relied on, as JSON. For AI review: confidence, evidence (the model's text), candidates (the refs shown, roster references by their roster ref), pins (the exact roster row each roster reference was read from) and run_id (ops.ai_spend). overridden_by ({method, versions, entity_id}) is added in a new row version when an active rule links the occurrence to something else.
evidence.blank_means: Empty object when there is none.

supersedes.meaning: The decision_id this decision replaces. The replaced decision is retired in the revision that made this one, and stays readable as of earlier revisions.

retired_reason.meaning: Why a decision stopped being in force, set with retired_revision_id.
retired_reason.blank_means: The decision is still in force.

asset_key.meaning: The fact-factory asset that published a row, such as sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants or entities/entities (docs/entity-registry-v1.md, "Asset layout"). The same key names the dataset in the public catalog. With acquisition, a spending table's asset_key names one slice of the table; on the derived tables it is the live slice's label (the occurrence source_key).

spending_key.meaning: The stable public key of one spending row (spending_store.spending_key, computed when the row is parsed): the first 128 bits of sha256 of the JSON array [asset_key, acquisition, resource_id, id], in Crockford base32 (26 characters, the ULID alphabet). Unique across a whole table (within one asset_key), unlike id, which is unique only per resource. Every parse of the same source row gives the same spending_key, so it is the same across publications and versions. Indexed (ix_spending_records_spending_key). Published references use gid://buildcanada/SpendingRecord/<spending_key>.

snapshot_id.meaning: A spending source's version: the largest committed spending_publications.version of the source when it was read (docs/STORAGE.md). Reading a (source, acquisition) slice at a version returns the publications committed at or before it and not replaced by then. A registry revision records the version each slice it resolved in full was read at (registry_revisions.inputs.slices), and derived_builds.slices the version of each live slice as of the build. On an occurrence, the version the occurrence version was resolved from; occurrence versions are not rewritten when unchanged, so versions resolved before the cut-over (2026-09-30) are Iceberg snapshot IDs, which no spending table can read.
snapshot_id.blank_means: The row is not from a spending source (registry rows).

capture_url.meaning: The public, content-addressed URL of a retained capture, <public base>/sha256/<first two characters>/<digest> (files.buildcanada.com once its custom domain is live). A key of the registry `source` JSON, defined here on its own.
capture_url.blank_means: The row was not parsed from a capture, or no public base URL was configured.

row_number.meaning: 1-based data row of the captured file a row was parsed from, header rows not counted. A key of the registry `source` JSON.
row_number.blank_means: The capture is not tabular, or the row predates row tracking.

name_fr.meaning: The French name StatCan gives a dimension or member.

redirected_to.meaning: The entity that now carries a redirected entity's record, set with status redirected (docs/entity-registry-v2.md, "Queue and redirects"; details in entities/entities).

position.meaning: 0-based position of an occurrence within a list-valued party field (recipients); 0 for single-valued fields. Part of the occurrence_id hash.

measure.meaning: What a source's amount measures (contract_value, aggregated_contract_value, agreement_value, payments_or_expenditure, award_amount, commitment). Amounts of different measures must never be added.

record_count.meaning: Spending rows counted in a summary group, latest revisions only and aggregate rows excluded.

agreement_count.meaning: Distinct canonical_id values among the rows counted in a summary group.

amount_missing_count.meaning: Rows counted in a summary group whose amount is blank. They add nothing to the group's amount.

aggregated_excluded.meaning: Rows of a summary group left out because they are aggregates (is_aggregated).

revisions_excluded.meaning: Rows of a summary group left out because a higher revision of the same canonical_id counts instead (revision_rank_json).

role.meaning: How a summarized entity takes part in the rows of a summary group. spending_summary, payer (field payer), research_org (field research_org) or recipient (every other party field); spending_counterparties, payer or recipient only (research_org is in neither role).

counterparty_id.meaning: The entity linked in the other role (payer for a recipient, recipient for a payer) on the counted rows of a spending_counterparties group. A row with two linked counterparties counts under each.
counterparty_id.blank_means: No counterparty is linked on those rows.

kind.meaning: Which of an entity version's names an entity_names row holds.

match_key.meaning: The exact-name search key of a name (entities/names.py match_key), under the names version in normalization. A query name keyed the same way finds the entities with that key; indexed (ix_entity_names_match_key).
match_key.blank_means: The name has no letters or digits to key.

normalization.meaning: The names version (entities/names.py NORMALIZATION_VERSION, such as names-v2) normalized_name and match_key were computed under.

institution_id.meaning: The registry entity ID of the municipality the document is filed under; for a province-wide document (scope province), the province's entity (buildcanada/jurisdictions:ca-xx), whose institutions row has status province.

document_type.meaning: What the document is said to be. Live captures from a website crawl are financial-report-candidate, an unverified finance-related PDF. A province-level collector's first capture takes the portal's type as a slug (audited-financial-statements, inspection-report, financial-statement, tax-rate-bylaw, financial-report); source_category has the label as published. A province-wide publication refiled under its province is provincial-publication. archive_import rows keep the legacy catalog's type (financial-statements, annual-report, statement-of-financial-information).

scope.meaning: province for a province-wide publication (a compilation or budget about every municipality), filed once under the province (`fact-factory documents refile-provincial`).

collector.meaning: The province-level collector that filed the document or captured its bytes again from a provincial portal (src/fact_factory/province_collectors.py) - sk-publications, ab-municipal-affairs or qc-mamh-financial-reports.
collector.blank_means: Found by the municipality's own website crawl, or an archive_import row not seen on a portal.

source_category.meaning: The document's type or category exactly as the provincial portal labels it ("Financial Statement", "Tax Rate Bylaw", "Saskatchewan Municipal Audited Financial Statements", "Municipal Inspection/Inquiry Reports", "Rapport financier et autres documents financiers"), for filtering by type.
source_category.blank_means: Not from a provincial portal (collector blank).

year.meaning: The fiscal year the document is about, as far as its metadata says. Archive rows: fiscal_period_end, else the year segment of the legacy canonical_id (".../financial-statements/2022/general"), else fiscal_period_start (financials.legacy_year). Live rows: the first year (1900 to next year) in the title, else the first in the URL file name, else the last in the URL folders; only the URL path counts, never its query string; digits inside a longer number are not a year; a URL year before 1990 is ignored; a full posting date in a file name counts only when nothing else names a year (municipal_ids.document_year, rule document-year-v2 since 2026-09-27). The municipal Dagster partition is this year when it is 2000 to 2030, else unknown.
year.blank_means: Neither the title nor the URL names a usable year, or the legacy entry gives none.
year.known_gaps: A multi-year plan or comparative statement takes its first year; nothing records its end year. Before document-year-v2 about 9,200 live rows had years from hashes, query strings and plan horizons; `fact-factory documents recompute-years` corrects existing rows and records each change in metadata.year_revisions.

url.meaning: The URL the document was downloaded from (live) or the legacy catalog's download URL (archive_import).

sha256.meaning: SHA-256 of the document's bytes, retained in R2 under sha256/<first two characters>/<digest>. One row per (institution_id, sha256).

text_sha256.meaning: SHA-256 of the gzipped JSON Lines page text extracted from the document, one line per page (document_id, source_sha256, page, text, parser_version).
text_sha256.blank_means: No text was extracted (state pending, needs_ocr or text_failed).

state.meaning: Where the document is in text extraction. pending: not yet extracted. text_ready: every page has text. text_partial: at least one page has under 40 characters (a cover or separator page is enough). needs_ocr: under 100 characters in all, so a scan with no text layer. text_failed: pdftotext could not read the file (a damaged or unsupported PDF; since 2026-09-27, with a text_failed case). None of these says the text is correct or complete.

rejected_reason.meaning: Warehouse only; never exported. Set when a maintenance rule decided the row is not its institution's document (`fact-factory documents reject`). off_domain_search_result: found on a search-engine results page, on a host that is not the municipality's own. provincial_publication_copy: a province-wide publication on a shared provincial host filed under each municipality that linked it; metadata.rejection.province_document_id names the one row kept under the province (`fact-factory documents refile-provincial`). refile_reverted: a province row whose refiling was reverted. A rejected row keeps its bytes and text in R2, is left out of the documents export and of partition metadata, and metadata.rejection records the rule, source page and time.

product_id.meaning: Statistics Canada's product ID (PID) of a table (cube), eight digits; the first two are its subject (14 labour, 18 prices, 98 census). The table's page is https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=<product_id>01, and its number as StatCan writes it is 14-10-0287-01.

ref_date.meaning: REF_DATE, the reference period a datapoint describes, exactly as published. Its form follows the table's frequency, such as 2026-08 (monthly), 2025 (annual), 1997/1998 (fiscal year) or 2021-05-11.

geo.meaning: GEO, the member of the table's first dimension (its geography, such as Canada or Ontario, or another first dimension StatCan labels GEO), in English.

dguid.meaning: DGUID, Statistics Canada's Dissemination Geography Unique Identifier of the geography, such as 2021A000011124 (Canada) or 2021A000235 (Ontario).
dguid.blank_means: The geography has no DGUID (some older or non-standard geographies).

statcan_dimension.meaning: One column per dimension of the table after the first: the dimension member, in English, exactly as the CSV writes it. The column name is the dimension name in snake case (Labour force characteristics becomes labour_force_characteristics; a name taken already gets a suffix); the Iceberg column doc and the dimensions table give the name as published.

uom.meaning: UOM, the unit of measure of the value, such as Persons, Dollars, Percentage or 2002=100.
uom.blank_means: Census tables, whose CSV has no unit column.

uom_id.meaning: UOM_ID, StatCan's code for the unit of measure (getCodeSets, uom).

scalar_factor.meaning: SCALAR_FACTOR, the multiplier the value is expressed in (units, thousands, millions, ...). The value is not multiplied by it.

scalar_id.meaning: SCALAR_ID, the scalar factor's code, the power of ten (0 units, 3 thousands, 6 millions, 9 billions).

vector.meaning: VECTOR, the StatCan identifier of the time series (a v followed by up to 10 digits), which never changes.
vector.blank_means: Census tables, and series StatCan publishes without a vector.

coordinate.meaning: COORDINATE, the member ID of each dimension, in dimension order, joined by dots (15.1, or 1.2.3.1.1.1). With product_id it identifies a series; with ref_date it identifies a datapoint (the check coordinates_unique). Census tables get the CSV's coordinate with the member ID of the value column's dimension appended.

symbol.meaning: SYMBOL, StatCan's symbol on the datapoint as published (p preliminary, r revised); in census tables, the Symbol column after the value.

terminated.meaning: TERMINATED as published; t when the series is terminated (no longer updated).

decimals.meaning: DECIMALS, the number of decimals StatCan states for the value.

source_row.meaning: The 1-based data row of the capture's CSV the row came from (the header and blank lines are not counted).

source_column.meaning: Census tables, the 0-based CSV column of the value cell the row came from (the Symbol column is the next one).
source_column.blank_means: Long tables, where a CSV row is one datapoint.

capture_sha256.meaning: SHA-256 of the full-table CSV zip (the capture) the row was parsed from, stored unchanged in R2 under sha256/<first two characters>/<sha256>.

dimension_position_id.meaning: The 1-based position of a dimension in its table (1 is the geography, GEO); a coordinate's n-th part is a member of dimension n.
dimension_position_id.blank_means: In footnotes, 0 when the footnote is attached to the whole table.

name_en.meaning: The English name StatCan gives a dimension or member.

has_uom.meaning: Whether the dimension's members carry the unit of measure (hasUom).

members.meaning: How many members the dimension has in the metadata.

member_id.meaning: A member's ID within its dimension (memberId); in footnotes, the member the footnote is attached to.
member_id.blank_means: In footnotes, 0 when attached to a whole dimension or table.

parent_member_id.meaning: The member's parent in its dimension's hierarchy (parentMemberId), such as Canada for a province.

classification_code.meaning: The member's code in a standard classification (classificationCode), such as an SGC province code (35) or a NAICS code.

classification_type_code.meaning: StatCan's code for the classification the classification_code belongs to (getCodeSets, classificationType).

geo_level.meaning: A geography member's level (geoLevel), 0 for the top.

member_terminated.meaning: Whether StatCan marks the member terminated (no longer used).

uom_code.meaning: The member's unit of measure code (memberUomCode), in dimensions with has_uom.

footnote_id.meaning: The footnote's number within its table.

release_time.meaning: When Statistics Canada released the table's current data, from WDS (releaseTime, 08:30 Eastern unless a correction), as a UTC timestamp (epoch seconds in the statcan_tables export). The date the source says it published, distinct from retrieved_at (when we fetched it) and published_at (when we published it).

metadata_sha256.meaning: SHA-256 of the getCubeMetadata JSON the row, or the table's release, was built from, stored unchanged in R2 under sha256/<first two>/<sha256>.

sources/ca/tbs/proactive_contracts.canonical_id: Hash of owner_org and procurement_id, falling back to reference_number when procurement_id is missing or a placeholder.
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_contracts.payer: The English part of owner_org_title, else of buyer_name, else owner_org. Every row had an owner_org_title on 2026-09-28.
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_contracts.value_consistent: contract_value = original_value + amendment_value (a blank amendment_value is 0); blank when contract_value or original_value is blank.
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_contracts.recipient_postal_code: vendor_postal_code. Only the forward sortation area (A1A) is published.
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_contracts.amount: contract_value. The contract's reported value, not payments made.
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_contracts.title: description_en, else description_fr. Blank when the source gives neither; the vendor name is only in `recipient`.
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_contracts.fiscal_year: The fiscal year of reporting_period (its first year, as in "2019-2020-Q4" or "2018/19 Q2"), not of the contract itself, which can be earlier when a contract is reported late. Where reporting_period names no year ("Q1", "A", "C") or is blank, the fiscal year (April to March) containing contract_date. Since parser spending-iceberg-v4; earlier snapshots are blank for periods without a year and use contract_date's calendar year otherwise.

sources/ca/tbs/aggregated_contracts.payer: The English part of owner_org_title. Before spending-iceberg-v5, the owner_org code.
sources/ca/tbs/aggregated_contracts.amount: Sum of the goods, services and construction original and amendment values plus acquisition card transactions. Known defect. A missing component is counted as 0.

sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants.external_id: Hash of owner_org, ref_number and amendment_number. Each amendment is its own row.
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants.payer: The English part of owner_org_title, else owner_org.
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants.recipient: recipient_legal_name, else recipient_operating_name. Legal names are often bilingual, joined by "|".
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants.recipient_type: recipient_type. Codes from the open.canada.ca grants schema: A Indigenous recipients, F For-profit organizations, G Government, I International (non-government), N Not-for-profit organizations and charities, O Other, P Individual or sole proprietorships, S Academia. Required only for agreements starting on or after 2025-12-01.
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants.amount: agreement_value for that amendment. Do not sum across rows sharing a canonical_id.
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants.program: prog_name_en, else prog_name_fr. Since parser spending-iceberg-v4.
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants.date: agreement_start_date. The spreadsheet placeholders 1899-12-30, 1899-12-31 and 1900-01-01 are blank; date_raw keeps them.
sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants.fiscal_year: The fiscal year (April to March) containing agreement_start_date, named by the calendar year it starts in. Blank when the date is blank or a placeholder. Since parser spending-iceberg-v4; earlier snapshots hold the calendar year of the start date.

sources/ca/pspc/transfer_payments.external_id: Hash of the entire source row. Any change to any source value produces a new identity.
sources/ca/pspc/transfer_payments.amount: Known defect. The first non-zero of aggregate payments (AGRG_PYMT_AMT) and current-year expenditure (TOT_CY_XPND_AMT), with the order depending on whether the row is an aggregate. Which measure was used is not recorded.
sources/ca/pspc/transfer_payments.fiscal_year: FSCL_YR, else the year in the CKAN resource name.
sources/ca/pspc/transfer_payments.is_aggregated: A blank recipient, or one containing "payments under", "name(s) withheld" or a count of recipients or payees ("(62 recipients)"). Since parser spending-iceberg-v4, which added the last two; an aggregate takes current-year expenditure first for `amount`.
sources/ca/pspc/transfer_payments.recipient_city: CTY_EN_NM or City_Ville_eng (English), else CTY_FR_NM or City_Ville_fra (French). Older files use the capitalized names, current files the bilingual ones.
sources/ca/pspc/transfer_payments.payer: DEPT_EN_DESC or Dept-name_Nom-min_eng, else the minister's portfolio (MINE, Min-portfolio_Portefeuille-min_eng).
sources/ca/pspc/transfer_payments.payer_code: Always blank. The files carry no organization code.

sources/ca/nserc/awards.external_id: Hash of the application ID and fiscal year. Batch-report aggregate rows without an ID use a hash of the row.
sources/ca/nserc/awards.payer: Always "Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada" ("NSERC" before spending-iceberg-nserc-v6).
sources/ca/nserc/awards.payer_code: Always nserc-crsng, NSERC's owner_org in the proactive grants and contracts tables.
sources/ca/nserc/awards.note: Text columns are trimmed since parser spending-iceberg-nserc-v5; raw_json keeps the values as published.

sources/ca/sshrc/awards.external_id: Hash of the SSHRC key (clé) and fiscal year. A batch-report row without a key uses a hash of the row.
sources/ca/sshrc/awards.payer: Always "Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada" ("SSHRC" before spending-iceberg-v5).
sources/ca/sshrc/awards.note: "Batch report | Report en lots" rows are aggregates (is_aggregated, recipient "Multiple recipients", no principal_investigator) since parser spending-iceberg-v4, which also trims text columns; raw_json keeps the values as published.

sources/ca/cihr/awards.payer: Always "Canadian Institutes of Health Research" ("CIHR" before spending-iceberg-v5).
sources/ca/cihr/awards.note: The Solr feed escapes accents as HTML entities ("Université Laval") and wraps abstracts in <html><body>. Published text is decoded as for every source (text_columns); raw_json keeps the escaped original.
sources/ca/cihr/awards.recipient: orgname, else orgnameinp2 (the institution paid). "Direct Payment" means the award was paid to the researcher, not to an institution; it is not an organization name.
sources/ca/cihr/awards.principal_investigator: name, the nominated principal investigator. pinamesdelim, all principal investigators, stays in raw_json.
sources/ca/cihr/awards.fiscal_year: Year of the competition date, minus one for January to March.

sources/ca/gac/iati_activities.payer_code: Always dfatd-maecd, Global Affairs Canada's owner_org.
sources/ca/gac/iati_activities.recipient: Not populated. Implementing organizations are in `recipients`.
sources/ca/gac/iati_activities.recipients: The English narrative, else the first narrative, of each participating-org with role 4 (implementing).
sources/ca/gac/iati_activities.recipient_refs: participating-org/@ref of the same role 4 organizations, in the same order.
sources/ca/gac/iati_activities.amount: Sum of commitment transactions (IATI type 2) when all are in one currency; blank otherwise. These are commitments, not spending. Known defect. A transaction with an empty value is counted as 0.
sources/ca/gac/iati_activities.date: iso-date of the first activity-date of type 2 (actual start) that is an ISO date, else of type 1 (planned start). date_raw is that iso-date as written. Blank when neither is present.
sources/ca/gac/iati_activities.fiscal_year: The Government of Canada fiscal year (April to March) containing `date`, named by the calendar year it starts in. The date's year, minus one for January to March, so 2025-02-01 is 2024 and 2025-04-15 is 2025. This is the convention CIHR uses and NSERC's "2024-2025" labels give (2024). Blank when `date` is blank.

sources/municipal/documents/capture.note: One row per (institution_id, sha256): a PDF filed under a municipality. The catalog's documents export has columns id, institution_id, source_key, document_type, title, year, url, sha256, text_sha256, state, parser_version, acquisition, scope, collector and source_category, plus sha256_url and text_sha256_url, and leaves out rows with a rejected_reason. A website crawl files a document only when it or the page linking it is on the municipality's own host, never from a search engine or a shared provincial host; a province-level collector files what its portal lists under the municipality the portal names (src/fact_factory/source_policy.py, province_collectors.py). About 70,000 live rows copied before 2026-09-27 are province-wide Quebec and Saskatchewan publications filed under each municipality; `fact-factory documents refile-provincial --apply` keeps one row each under the province (scope province) and rejects the copies.
sources/municipal/documents/capture.id: An opaque document ID (a ULID for rows since the slug migration; older rows keep their original hash). Kept when the institution's key changes.
sources/municipal/documents/capture.acquisition: live for a collector's fetch; archive_import for a document registered from the legacy catalog (catalog/legacy-documents.jsonl.gz). Archive rows are historical evidence, not current coverage.
sources/municipal/documents/capture.title: Live: the link text on the page it was found on, else the file name; search-result rows carry the result snippet; a province-level collector's rows are the municipality as the portal names it, the year and the document type. Archive: the legacy title, else title_fr (since 2026-09-27).
sources/municipal/documents/capture.parser_version: The text extraction version (pdftotext-v1). Blank until extracted.

entities/entities.note: One row version per entity. Columns entity_id, anchor, entity_class, subtype, name, name_fr, aliases, jurisdiction, status, valid_from, valid_to, attributes and the registry bookkeeping columns.
entities/entities.name_fr: French name, where the roster gives one.
entities/entities.attributes: Roster-specific details as JSON, such as faa_schedule and institutional_form for federal bodies, municipality_type_raw for municipalities, or accounts (every CRA program account under the BN9, lowest BN15 first), category_code and sub_category_code (the CRA category and sub-category codes of the lowest BN15's row, such as 0100 and 0006) for charities. An Ontario agency carries classification, classification_2000, governance, cluster, public_body, website and ministry, and form and form_evidence where its crosswalk entry records a government business enterprise; a school board board_type, language, region, website and addresses. A federal predecessor carries institutional_form (TBS-style, by analogy with its successor), note, and authority, locator, citation_sha256 and citations for its dates. refined_bounds, on a TBS inventory entity, records a valid_from or valid_to the inventory gives only as a year and the curated roster gives to the day, with value, inventory_value (the year the inventory row still says), the roster row, and the citation. inventory_start_after_end and inventory_active_with_end keep a TBS inventory row's contradictory published values (see valid_from and status). status_inferred, on a GC organization code outside the inventory, says its status was read from a blank status_statut. On an entity merged by charity-merge-v1, merged holds rule, provincial_anchor and charity_anchor, and charity the charity's CRA details as they stand on a charity entity (name, subtype and status the charity alone would have, jurisdiction, category, category_code, sub_category_code, designation, city, postal_code, accounts, and the CRA row as source); the other attributes are the provincial record's. Since registry-build-v3 (charity-merge-v2) a municipality or Indigenous roster entity that absorbed a charity carries merged (rule, roster_anchor, charity_anchor) and charity the same way, and keeps its own attributes. identifier_evidence, on an Indigenous roster entity and, since registry-build-v4, on an ISC tribal council an identified row names, lists the curated row's cited identifiers (namespace, value, and citations, each a locator, sha256 and pinpoint on a checked-in excerpt of a Corporations Canada page, or roster_citation, which is a CRA List of charities row by roster, record_key and name, or a Corporations Canada row by roster ca/ised/federal_corporations, record_key (the corporation number), field (the column that gives the value) and name). cited_aliases, since federal-predecessors-v3 on a TBS inventory entity, lists the cited names the federal predecessors roster adds to its aliases (name, written_forms, authority, locator, citation_sha256, citations), such as the Office of Infrastructure of Canada on org 237.
entities/entities.valid_from: As published by the roster; for a TBS inventory entity with refined_bounds, the day its cited instrument gives.
entities/entities.valid_to: As published by the roster; for a federal predecessor, the day its cited instrument ended it; for a TBS inventory entity with refined_bounds, the day its cited instrument gives. Blank on a created entity.
entities/entities.redirected_to: A created entity a reviewed redirect decision retired in favour of the entity_id named here (the survivor); status is then redirected. Its occurrences link to the survivor from the next release, and a later correction reverses it. Since registry-build-v2 also a provincial roster entity whose record was merged into the charity entity that is the same body (charity-merge-v1; release 7 had built 140 such provincial entities beside their charities): it keeps its ID and anchor, loses its identifiers and relationships, and is never a name-match candidate. Since registry-build-v3 also a charity entity merged into the municipality or Indigenous roster entity that is the same body (charity-merge-v2: City of Surrey, Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami; since registry-build-v4, charity-merge-v3, also into an ISC tribal council: Windigo First Nations Council), and an Indigenous roster entity whose curated row is now a party or member row on an ISC entity (the Gwich'in Tribal Council, redirected to ISC tribal council 1034). The ID is never reused. Blank for every other entity.
entities/entities.created_entities: Entities with source.origin creation (docs/entity-registry-v2.md, "Entity creation") are made from spending rows, not rosters. anchor is ca.cra.bn9:<bn9> or org-id:<ref> for a unit with an identifier, else created:<ulid>, minted once and never recomputed. class is organization; subtype business (grants recipient_type F, or a legal-form suffix), non_profit (type N), foreign_org (type I), indigenous_org (type A) or unknown. attributes.observed holds what the rows show, as observation, not legal fact: first_row_date, last_row_date, provinces, countries, sources, occurrences and, for an identifier-free unit, place ({city} or {fsa}); attributes.created holds unit_key, rule (the create version that minted it: create-v2 counts distinct evidence; create-v4 reads the place from the city as creation.city_place does, so "Toronto | Toronto" and "Toronto, Ontario" are the city toronto, a province written after the city filling a blank province; create-v5 holds back a unit named as a roster entity only in that entity's province) and founded_release. valid_from is always blank and jurisdiction is set only from an identifier (ca for a BN9; the registry country of an org-id), since the rows give no evidence of either.

entities/identifiers.note: One row version per (entity_id, namespace, value).
entities/identifiers.valid_from: Blank. No roster says when a code was assigned.
entities/identifiers.valid_to: Since registry-build-v2, the valid_to of the entity it identifies (a code ends with its entity); blank for an entity with none. An LEI attached from GLEIF has no dates.

sources/ca-on/tbs/provincial_agencies.AEAD, 2010 Classification/AAD, 2015 Clas: Advisory, Adjudicative, Regulatory, Regulatory (governing board), Operational Service, Operational Enterprise or Trust; attributes.classification and part of the crosswalk label.
