sources/ca/nserc/eligible_institutions.note: One row per institution on NSERC's list of eligible institutions (HTML). The page states no licence (its footer is added by script), so the names are an index only: build.charity_subtype gives a teaching-institution charity subtype university when a name matches one in the Canadian Universities section after normalization, and catalog/nserc-charity-crosswalk.json (nserc-charity-v1) matches 80 of the 81 universities to the charity BN9 that is the institution (the legal names differ for 16, such as THE GOVERNING COUNCIL OF THE UNIVERSITY OF TORONTO); the matched charity gets subtype university, and resolution indexes the NSERC name as an exact-name key of that charity in its province (read from the pinned capture), so a spending row naming the university matches it. The NSERC name is never written to the entity: not an alias, not an attribute. The crosswalk keys rows by record key (section and name) and holds nothing else from the list. Not published as entities or rows of their own. Colleges are not crosswalked. The three affiliated research centres are listed outside the province blocks and are not read.
sources/ca/nserc/eligible_institutions.province: The province block the name is listed under.
sources/ca/nserc/eligible_institutions.name: The institution's name, without the trailing asterisk.
sources/ca/nserc/eligible_institutions.exceptional: true when the page marks the name with an asterisk (college eligibility granted on an exceptional basis), else blank.

sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.note: Corporations Canada's public record of each federal corporation (OGL-Canada), two responses per corporation number of the ca/ised/federal_corporations roster: the JSON API record (https://ised-isde.canada.ca/cc/lgcy/api/corporations/<number>.json?lang=eng) in warehouse.corporation_details, and the Federal corporation information page (https://ised-isde.canada.ca/cc/lgcy/fdrlCrpDtls.html?corpId=<number>&lang=eng) in warehouse.corporation_pages, each stored gzipped exactly as received (raw, sha256 of the uncompressed bytes, http_status, fetched_at) and never fetched again unless refreshed. Directors and individuals with significant control, shown only on the page, are parsed into warehouse.corporation_directors and warehouse.corporation_significant_control. The names and addresses are public under the CBCA, the NFP Act and the CBCA ISC register (public since 2024); they are published as Corporations Canada shows them. Partitioned by shard; each shard's responses are also archived to R2 as one gzip JSON-lines object (warehouse.corporation_detail_archives). docs/RUNBOOK.md, "Corporation records".
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.corporation_number: The Corporations Canada corporation number without its check digit, as the roster writes it (2493306, shown 249330-6 on the page); the key of every table.
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.outcome: found, or not_found (the API answers ["could not find corporation <n>", ...]; the page shows no corporation panel). A not_found response is stored and not fetched again.
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.corporation_id: The record's corporationId; equals corporation_number (check numbers_match).
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.status: The JSON status, more detailed than the roster's (Active, Dissolved, Inactive - Amalgamated, Inactive - Discontinued, Active - Dissolution Pending (Non-compliance), Active - Intent to Dissolve Filed ...).
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.act: Governing act, as written (Canada Business Corporations Act; Canada Not-for-profit Corporations Act; Canada Corporations Act - Part  II, with the source's double space).
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.bn9: The first nine digits of businessNumbers.businessNumber; blank when the record has none (common before about 1995).
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.incorporated_on: Date of the earliest Incorporation activity; blank for a corporation that came by continuance or amalgamation.
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.dissolved_on: Date of the latest activity starting "Dissolution", blank when a Revival is later ("Statement of Intent to Dissolve" is not a dissolution). Some old records say Dissolved with no Dissolution activity, so no date (2453, dissolved, Boards of Trade Act).
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.amalgamated_on: Date of the latest Amalgamation activity, the day this corporation was formed by amalgamating others. A corporation that amalgamated into another has status Inactive - Amalgamated and no dated activity for it (154768); its date is the successor's amalgamated_on, which the record does not link.
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.discontinued_on: Date of the latest Discontinuance (continued into another jurisdiction, named in the activity's jurisdictionId).
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.names: JSON list of corporationNames, unwrapped (name, nameType, current, effectiveDate, expiryDate).
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.activities: JSON list of activities, unwrapped (activity, date, and section or jurisdictionId where given).
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.annual_returns: JSON list of annualReturns, unwrapped (annualMeetingdate, yearOfFiling, typeOfCorporation).
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.directors: On corporation_pages, the number of directors the page lists.
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.significant_control: On corporation_pages, the number of individuals with significant control the page lists (current and previous).
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.isc_updated_on: On corporation_pages, the ISC panel's "Last updated or confirmed" date. The panel appears for CBCA business corporations only (not NFP Act or Canada Corporations Act ones), and in the smoke test of 2026-09-28 on 16 of 17 active CBCA corporations and none of 13 dissolved ones.
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.isc_note: On corporation_pages, the ISC panel's sentence when it lists nobody ("There are no individuals with significant control over the corporation.").
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.error: The last failed fetch's error (HTTP 500, a network error, or a 200 with an unexpected body), with error_status, error_at and error_raw (its body, gzipped, at most 64 KB). A stored response is never replaced by a failure; a success clears these.
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.archive_sha256: The R2 archive that holds the stored response; blank until the shard is archived.
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.note_directors: corporation_directors: one row per director listed on a stored page, in page order (position from 0): name and the address as the page shows it (address, lines joined by newlines; address_lines, a JSON list). Replaced when the page is refetched; page_sha256 names the page read.
sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.note_significant_control: corporation_significant_control: one row per individual with significant control on a stored page: current (1 under "Current individuals", 0 under a previous list), name, address_label ("Address for service" when the page labels the address so; blank means the address shown, which the corporation filed), address and address_lines, interest (Type of interest or control), holds_shares (Directly or Indirectly), control (Individually or Jointly), holding (the share band, such as At least 25% and up to 50% of the shares), start_date and end_date where shown, and fields, every label and value of the entry as shown.

sources/ca/ised/federal_corporation_deta.note: corporation_detail_plan: one row per corporation number of the roster's latest capture set when planned, with tier (1 a BN9 some current registry occurrence carries as ca.cra.bn9, that is a grants recipient_business_number; 2 a roster reference of a current occurrence, roster_refs, or a registry entity anchored on the number; 3 Dissolved or Inactive in the roster; 4 the rest), shard (t<tier>-<nnnn>, 5,000 numbers, in number order within a tier), capture_id, bn9, roster_status and planned_at. A number keeps its tier and shard when the plan is extended by a later capture. Each shard is a work row (work, kind fetch, family corporations, key corporations:<shard>) holding its size, runs and completion.

entities/relationships.note: One row version per (subject_id, predicate, object_id, object_ref). valid_from is not part of the key, so a relationship that ends and later holds again (an ownership re-acquired) cannot be two rows yet.
entities/relationships.valid_from: Since registry-build-v2: for succeeded_by, the effective_date of the succession; for party_to, the agreement's effective_date; for located_within, and for controlled_by on basis statute (a body its enabling instrument makes a controlled body), the subject's valid_from. Blank for the rest, whose sources give no start: owned_by and controlled_by from Crown holdings, reports_to_minister (a lead department), member_of (ISC's association file has no dates; since registry-build-v3 a curated member row starts at its government's valid_from, which only the Tlicho Government has: 2005-08-04), governs, covers. Blank before registry-build-v2.
entities/relationships.valid_to: Since registry-build-v2, the subject's valid_to (no link outlives its subject), except succeeded_by, which never ends. Blank for a subject with none, and before registry-build-v2.

entities/mention_occurrences.note: One row version per occurrence_id. snapshot_id is the spending version the row was read from (an Iceberg snapshot ID before 2026-09-30); spending_row_id is the spending table's id column; position is the index within an array field such as GAC recipients, else 0. Until a rule's (method, versions) pair is activated from a gold set, no rule links, so entity_id is blank on every occurrence (0 of 12,313,634 in release 11), and a rule's match is reason proposed with the proposed entity first in candidates, so consumers read candidates[0] of a proposed occurrence, whose precision is not yet measured. Retention. Only the versions current in the last published release are kept (FACT_FACTORY_REGISTRY_KEEP_RELEASES, default 1). After each publish, fact-factory entities prune deletes every version retired in or before K, the last published release (releases.prune; decided 2026-09-29, no archive). An older release is marked pruned (warehouse.registry_releases.pruned_at) and its occurrences as of that release are incomplete, so it is not reproducible from the warehouse, and the gold set, activation, AI review and creation samples refuse it.
entities/mention_occurrences.province: Lowercase two-letter province code from the spending row, when it maps.
entities/mention_occurrences.city: The party's city as the spending row publishes it (recipient_city), trimmed. Blank when the source gives none, and on a research_org occurrence, since the row's city describes the recipient.
entities/mention_occurrences.postal_code: The party's postal code when it is a complete Canadian code, uppercase without spaces (A1A1A1). Blank when the source gives none, gives only the forward sortation area, gives a malformed value, or the party is outside Canada.
entities/mention_occurrences.fsa: The forward sortation area (A1A), the first three characters of postal_code, or a bare FSA as the source publishes it (proactive_contracts). Blank when the source gives neither.
entities/mention_occurrences.kind_reason: Why the party got its party_kind, as entities/occurrences.py decides it: grants_recipient_type_<code> (the grants recipient_type A, F, G, I, N, O, P or S), grants_researcher_name_type_<code> (since occurrences-v5: a recipient written as a researcher, "Surname, Given" or "Surname, Given-Institution", under an organization type, which is an individual; about 7,000 grants rows in release 7, over 99% of the 4,867 distinct names persons on review, the rest mostly type N "Name, Place" organizations), payer_field, institution_field, blank_name, blank_type_org_marker, blank_type_person_name_rule, blank_type_unsure_default_organization (since occurrences-v7: the person rule is unsure, so the party is an organization candidate; about 50 of 80 such names sampled in release 8 were organizations), blank_type_unsure_default_individual (the same case until occurrences-v6, excluded as an individual), withheld_name (since occurrences-v7: the name is only a withheld-name label such as REDACTED, Name withheld or Payment made to individual / Paiement émis à un individu, an individual whatever the recipient type), blank_type_roster_name (since occurrences-v6: the name equals, normalized, a current non-charity roster organization's name, such as Nunavut Tunngavik; since occurrences-v8 every name of an ISC First Nation, tribal council or Indigenous government counts, such as Mistawasis Nêhiyawak) and so on. Since occurrences-v8 a name written the same on both sides of "|" (Charles McCardle|Charles McCardle) is classified as its one side, and Secretariat is an organization word. Since occurrences-v7 a "Surname, Given" name in any case (SANDHU, MANJIT SINGH) is blank_type_person_name_rule. Since occurrences-v6 people named together need each side to be a person's name, so a trade or institution name joined by & is an organization; researcher names accept surname particles and lower-case names followed by an institution, and not foreign institution words or a legal form after the comma (Instituto Blacksmith México, A.C.). Since occurrences-v5 the person rule also marks an organization by a trade, community or Indigenous word (occurrences.TRADE_WORDS) unless the name also names a person ("Chad Parr Painting"), by a partnership or foreign legal form (GP, s.e.c., Sdn Bhd), or by an English and a French name joined by "|"; a title (Dr., Mr.) or a "Last, First (Affiliation)" name is an individual. On 8,286 blank-type excluded_individual rows sampled from release 7, 1,682 (1,022 names) became organizations, none of them a person's given name and surname; on 20,443 blank_type_org_marker rows, 121 became individuals, 119 of them researchers written "Last, First (University)". Entity creation reads the recipient type from it.
entities/mention_occurrences.country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the row places the party in (CA when a province maps and no country is given); blank where the source gives neither. For GAC recipients it is blank, since the field naming the recipient's country is unverified.
entities/mention_occurrences.create_unit: For an unlinked or created-member organization occurrence, its entity creation unit: its identifier (ca.cra.bn9:<bn9>, else org-id:<ref>), or name: followed by the JSON list [normalized name, province, place kind, place], place being the normalized city, else the FSA. Blank when the occurrence has neither an identifier nor a place, and for every other occurrence.
entities/mention_occurrences.create_reason: For an unlinked no_candidate organization occurrence (or one fuzzy review left ai_undecided), why creation made no entity for its unit: too_few (fewer than three occurrences across two fiscal years or two sources, and no identifier; since create-v2 occurrences are counted as distinct evidence, so an archive-imported copy of a live row, the same spending row under <source>@archive_import, counts once, and so does a content copy of a row in one snapshot, a row with source_occurrence above 1 whose content equals an earlier row's), single_token, person_rule (a name the person rule calls an individual; since occurrences-v7 a name it is unsure of is not one), pending_review (fuzzy candidates awaiting AI review), identifier_held (another entity holds its identifier), identifier_conflict (names disagree under one identifier; queued), namesake_of_identified (its name and province belong to an identified unit; listed), namesake_unplaced (no city or FSA), roster_gap (government, academic or marker-word units, and since create-v4 units with a member whose name is a current roster entity's name, French name or alias, such as a federal body named in a recipient field; since create-v5 only in that entity's province when it has one, the row's province being its own, its city field's or its FSA's; this test comes before too_few and single_token; they go to fuzzy review and the roster gap list, never to creation) or rule_inactive (the unit passes the create rule but the create pair is not active: a proposal). Blank for every other occurrence.
entities/mention_occurrences.row_date: The row's date under its source's date rule; see SOURCE_DATE_RULES in entities/occurrences.py.
entities/mention_occurrences.identifiers: Validated identifiers from the row as JSON, by namespace. Since occurrences-v9 an individual occurrence keeps its identifiers too (a sole proprietor's business number, or an institution's BN written on a researcher's row); before, they were removed. Resolution excludes every individual before reading identifiers, so an individual's identifier never links it to an entity.
entities/mention_occurrences.roster_refs: For each candidate that is a roster reference (ca/ised/federal_corporations:<number>, a corporation with no entity yet, or first linked in this release), the roster row the release read, as JSON: {ref: {source_key, record_key, capture_id, row_sha256}}. row_sha256 is the digest of that row's record (rosters.row_sha256). Blank when no candidate is a roster reference.
entities/mention_occurrences.row_context: For an occurrence the rules left conflict or ambiguous, what AI review is shown from the spending row, as JSON: payer, program and description, each where the source publishes it (published columns payer, program, description). Never the amount. Blank for every other occurrence.
entities/mention_occurrences.review_unit_id: For an occurrence the rules left conflict or ambiguous, its AI review unit key: the SHA-256 of everything the reviewer is shown (source, field, raw name, identifiers, province, city, postal code or FSA, period key, row_context, and each candidate with its pinned version: an entity's row_id in the release, or a roster reference's pin). Occurrences with the same key share one review. The period key is the fiscal year, or the row date where a candidate's validity changes inside that year. Also set for a no_candidate organization occurrence that has fuzzy_candidates, whose unit holds those candidates marked fuzzy and is reviewed under the fuzzy-v1 pair. Blank for every other occurrence.
entities/mention_occurrences.evidence_sha256: The SHA-256 of what the rules computed for the occurrence before decisions (resolve.evidence_digest, evidence-v1): its extracted fields and the rules' outcome, every candidate they found, the roster rows pinned for them and the payer attribution. Bookkeeping for incremental resolution: a build that computes the same digest for an occurrence that no decision names, that is not a review unit and whose fuzzy search cannot find anything new keeps the row version as it is. Blank on row versions written before incremental resolution.
entities/mention_occurrences.fuzzy_candidates: For a no_candidate organization occurrence whose normalized name has a municipal, university, hospital or First Nation marker word (goldset.MARKER_WORDS), its fuzzy-v1 candidates as a JSON list of refs, best first, at most 8: records sharing the name's rarest token in the release's token index, ranked by token overlap (Jaccard). A charity or First Nation is named by its entity ID; a federal corporation by its roster reference, pinned in roster_refs. Shown to AI review only, under the pair with candidate_generator fuzzy-v1; no rule links on them. Blank for every other occurrence.

entities/mentions.note: Current state. One row per (source_key, field, raw_name) of the current occurrences with occurrences (count), linked (count linked; proposals are not links) and entity_ids (distinct entities linked); a slice's rows are rebuilt by each revision that writes or retires its occurrences, and revision_id names that revision.

entities/resolution_decisions.note: One row per decision, versioned like the other registry tables (row_id, content_sha256, source, recorded_at, revision_id, retired_revision_id). A decision is in force in the revisions between revision_id and retired_revision_id; a replacement names it in supersedes, and no decision is edited. Columns decision_id, subject, subject_kind, outcome, entity_id, entity_ref, decider, versions, input_sha256, evidence, supersedes and retired_reason. AI review decisions are written by resolution revisions from stored answers (fact-factory entities ai-review), one per occurrence of a review unit. Creation writes one created_member decision (decider rule, versions the create pair, input_sha256 the digest of the occurrence's create_unit, evidence unit_key and founding) per occurrence that joins a created entity; entity-level decisions (subject_kind entity, subject a created entity) are redirect (entity_id the survivor; by a reviewer, or by the redirect pair once active), correction (a reviewer keeping the entity, which reverses a redirect) and same_as (entity_ref.ref a roster record that covers the entity and attaches to its ID). A decision can have several row versions (overridden_by is added in a new one); decision_id stays.
entities/resolution_decisions.source: The decider as origin, such as {"origin": "ai"}.

sources/ca/statcan/t_<productId>.note: Pending a PostgreSQL design (2026-09-30): not loaded; as designed with Iceberg: One Iceberg table per Statistics Canada table (cube), sources.ca.statcan.t_<product_id>, from its English full-table CSV (WDS getFullTableDownloadCSV). One row per datapoint: unique by (coordinate, ref_date), checked on every load (coordinates_unique). A long table's rows equal StatCan's nbDatapointsCube. Census tables (product IDs 98...) are published wide; each value cell is one row. Replaced whole at each StatCan release; earlier releases are earlier snapshots. Columns: product_id, ref_date, geo, dguid, one statcan_dimension column per further dimension, uom, uom_id, scalar_factor, scalar_id, vector, coordinate, value, status, symbol, terminated, decimals, source_row, source_column, capture_sha256. Licence: Statistics Canada Open Licence.
sources/ca/statcan/t_<productId>.statcan_dimension: The columns between dguid and uom. Census tables also get one for the dimension their value columns spread across (such as sex_3).
sources/ca/statcan/t_<productId>.known_gaps: uom, uom_id, scalar_factor, scalar_id, vector, terminated and decimals are blank in census tables, whose CSV has no such columns; members.uom_code has the unit of each member of a dimension with has_uom. English labels only; French names are in sources/ca/statcan/members and dimensions.

sources/ca/statcan/dimensions.note: One row per dimension of each loaded table, from the getCubeMetadata JSON of the release its table holds; unique by (product_id, dimension_position_id). Partitioned by product_id, each table's partition replaced whole. Columns product_id, dimension_position_id, name_en, name_fr, has_uom, members, release_time, metadata_sha256.

sources/ca/statcan/members.note: One row per member of each dimension of each loaded table, unique by (product_id, dimension_position_id, member_id). Columns product_id, dimension_position_id, member_id, parent_member_id, name_en, name_fr, classification_code, classification_type_code, geo_level, vintage, member_terminated, uom_code, metadata_sha256.
sources/ca/statcan/members.vintage: The geography vintage of a geography member (vintage), such as 2021, as a string.

sources/ca/statcan/footnotes.note: One row per footnote of each loaded table and member it is attached to (a footnote attached to several members is several rows). Columns product_id, footnote_id, text_en, text_fr, dimension_position_id and member_id (0 and 0 for the whole table), metadata_sha256.

sources/ca/statcan/cubes.note: The WDS listing (getAllCubesListLite), one record per table, kept in PostgreSQL (statcan_cubes) with every listing captured in R2; not an Iceberg table. The checked-in catalog/statcan-cubes.json is its slowly changing part (product ID, CANSIM ID, titles, subject and survey codes, frequency, archived) and defines the assets. Between midnight and 08:30 Eastern the listing leaves out tables locked for the day's release.

statcan_tables.note: Not exported since 2026-09-30 (StatCan storage pending a PostgreSQL design); as it was: The public catalog export (statcan_tables.jsonl.gz), one row per loaded StatCan table at the snapshot it is published at. id is the Iceberg identifier (sources.ca.statcan.t_<product_id>), not a spending row id. Columns product_id, title_en, title_fr, subject_code, frequency_code, archived, release_time, retrieved_at (when we fetched the zip, epoch seconds), source_url (the WDS zip URL), table_url (the table's page at StatCan), csv_sha256 and metadata_sha256 (each with a _url to the stored bytes), layout (long or wide), rows, snapshot_id, metadata_location, metadata_url, parser_version, release_key (SHA-256 of product, csv_sha256 and parser version), published_at (when we published it, epoch seconds), licence (statcan-open-licence) and delisted_at (when WDS stopped listing the table, epoch seconds; blank while listed; the table stays published with its history).
statcan_tables.archived: WDS archiveStatusCode as published, 2 current and 1 archived (no longer updated).
statcan_tables.frequency_code: WDS frequencyCode (getCodeSets, frequency), such as 6 monthly, 9 quarterly, 12 annual.

statcan_normalized/t_<productId>.note: Pending a PostgreSQL design (2026-09-30): not loaded; as designed with Iceberg: One Iceberg table per StatCan table except the census (98-) tables, which are not normalized, statcan_normalized.t_<product_id>, built from the raw table's current snapshot (sources/ca/statcan/t_<productId>, which stays as published and is what to cite). Every raw row and column, in the raw order and under the raw names (a dimension column whose name a derived column takes gets the suffix _dimension), then period_start, period_end, frequency, value_scaled, unit, status_label, is_suppressed, is_unreliable, is_missing, is_rounded_zero, quality_grade, is_preliminary, is_revised, is_terminated, dguid_vintage, dguid_type, dguid_schema, geo_level, sgc_code, province, entity_id, entity_match, registry_release_id, and a statcan_member_id and a statcan_code column per dimension (geo_member_id, geo_code, then <dimension column>_member_id and _code). Replaced whole at each build; the snapshot summary names the raw release and snapshot, the registry release and the normalizer version. Licence: Statistics Canada Open Licence (adapted data).
statcan_normalized/t_<productId>.entity_id: The registry entity of the row's geography, as entity_match says; blank when not linked.

statcan/series.note: Pending a PostgreSQL design (2026-09-30): not loaded; as designed with Iceberg: One row per StatCan vector across every table, statcan.series, partitioned by product_id (each table's slice replaced at its build) and sorted by vector. Census (98-) tables are not normalized, so they are not here. Unique by vector (vectors_unique). Columns product_id, title, vector, coordinate, series_name, dimension_members, classification_codes, unit, scalar_id, scalar_factor, frequency, dguid, geo_level, province, sgc_code, entity_id, entity_match, first_ref_date, last_ref_date, first_period_start, last_period_end, observations, is_terminated, release_time, raw_snapshot_id, capture_sha256, registry_release_id. The attributes of the series' first row (unit, scalar, geography) are the series' own; StatCan gives each vector one.
statcan/series.entity_id: The registry entity of the series' geography.
statcan/series.release_time: When StatCan released the table data the series was built from.
statcan/series.capture_sha256: The raw capture (full-table zip) the series was built from.

statcan/observations.note: Pending a PostgreSQL design (2026-09-30): not loaded; as designed with Iceberg: One row per StatCan datapoint across every table except the census (98-) tables, which are not normalized, statcan.observations: the rows of every normalized table, fewer columns. Partitioned by product_id (each table's slice replaced at its build); within a slice sorted by vector, then period_start. For one series, read statcan/series for its product_id and filter both; for one entity, read the series with that entity_id, then their product_ids and vectors. Columns product_id, vector, coordinate, ref_date, period_start, period_end, frequency, value, value_scaled, scalar_id, unit, status, status_label, is_suppressed, is_unreliable, is_missing, is_rounded_zero, quality_grade, is_preliminary, is_revised, is_terminated, dguid, geo_level, province, sgc_code, entity_id, entity_match, capture_sha256, source_row, registry_release_id.

statcan_normalized/tables.note: The Dagster asset standing for every statcan_normalized.t_<productId> table (one asset, not one per table); its checks cover the tables a run built.

statcan_normalized.note: Not exported since 2026-09-30 (StatCan storage pending a PostgreSQL design); as it was: The public catalog export (statcan_normalized.jsonl.gz), one row per StatCan table with a published normalized build. id is the Iceberg identifier (statcan_normalized.t_<product_id>). Columns product_id, release_key, normalizer_version, registry_release_id, raw_snapshot_id, table_snapshot_id, series_snapshot_id, observations_snapshot_id, rows, series, published_at.

publication/derived_tables.note: Tables the public API reads beside the registry and spending tables, because they are too slow to compute per request (src/fact_factory/derived.py; docs/RUNBOOK.md, "Derived tables"). They follow the registry's head: each build (entity_registry_job, registry_daily_job or derived_tables_job) brings them from the last build point to the head in one transaction, and its derived_builds row is written last, so a reader that sees revision N there sees all of it. entity_names, spending_summary and spending_counterparties are versioned like the registry tables: a row is current as of revision N when revision_id <= N and (retired_revision_id is blank or retired_revision_id > N). Spending rows as of N are those of the version each live slice was last resolved in full at. The blocking checks summary_reconciles (up to 200 sampled entities recomputed in Python) and names_cover_entities run before the derived_builds row is written; a failure writes nothing. york_factory reads these and every other fact-factory table directly, as the read-only role api_reader; there is no serving copy (since 2026-09-30).
publication/derived_tables.derived_builds: One row per build point: revision_id (the registry revision the tables were brought up to), previous_revision_id (the build before it; blank for the first), slices (per live slice label, such as sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants: the spending version it was read at, blank when nothing is published), counts (rows added and retired per table, and the entities whose summaries were recomputed; entities is blank on a full rebuild), checks (the blocking checks with their metadata), build_version, built_at (Unix seconds) and build_seconds. A slice last resolved at a version the spending tables cannot read (an Iceberg snapshot ID) holds builds back until it resolves again (fact-factory derived status).
publication/derived_tables.entity_names: One row per name, French name or alias of an entity version (entities.row_id): kind (name, name_fr or alias), name as published, normalized_name (names.normalize), match_key and normalization, with the entity_id and the entity version's revision_id and retired_revision_id. Exact-name search reads match_key. Written for each entity version a revision adds; a retired version's names are retired with it.
publication/derived_tables.spending_summary: One row per (entity_id, role, asset_key, fiscal_year, currency), versioned by revision_id and retired_revision_id (a build recomputes only the entities linked to a changed row, retiring their rows), under fixed rules: only linked (entity_id set) live occurrences, never archive_import; one row per source, never summed across sources; role payer, recipient (recipient, recipients and vendor_name fields) or research_org; a live record held in several resources counts once; where the table ranks revisions (revision_rank_json), only the highest-ranked revision per canonical_id counts. record_count, agreement_count, amount (sum of the counted amounts in currency; blank when none has an amount, never 0 for missing), amount_missing_count, aggregated_excluded (is_aggregated rows left out), revisions_excluded (lower revisions left out). measure names what amount measures: contract_value (proactive contracts), aggregated_contract_value, agreement_value (grants: not money paid), payments_or_expenditure (transfer payments), award_amount (NSERC, SSHRC, CIHR) or commitment (GAC). source_key is the adapter. id is a surrogate key.
publication/derived_tables.spending_counterparties: The spending summary split by counterparty, versioned as the summary is: for each entity linked as payer (field payer) or recipient (fields recipient, recipients, principal_investigator, vendor_name) on live rows, the linked entity in the other role on the same row (counterparty_id; blank when none is linked, and a row with two linked counterparties counts under each), with the summary's rules, measures and columns (record_count, agreement_count, amount, amount_missing_count, aggregated_excluded, revisions_excluded). research_org is in neither role. Precomputed so group_by=counterparty is a lookup.

publication/public_catalog.note: catalog/latest.json points at the current index.json (content-addressed). Since 2026-09-29 a run whose index content (everything but generated_at) equals the latest one's publishes nothing, and each published index is appended to catalog_history and catalog/history.json (entries index_sha256, url, visible_from in Unix seconds and visible_from_utc; the catalog current at a time T is the last entry with visible_from <= T; before the first entry nothing was recorded). Since 2026-09-30 the index lists raw_captures (the content-addressed key, sha256/<first two characters>/<sha256>, its public URL prefix, and the exports that list them: spending_snapshots and documents) and api (the public API, to come); no Iceberg tables, releases or StatCan exports. The index adds history (its URL and rule) and dictionary (catalog/dictionary.json, the machine-readable export of this file, and its sha256; also listed under exports as dictionary.json).

elections/captures.note: Every source response the elections pipeline stored in R2, one row per distinct set of bytes (the candidate list PDF, the voting information page, the boundary files, the 2024 results CSV, the results container listing and pages, and each page the contact research and verification captured). Fetching the same bytes again only moves last_retrieved_at. Raw captures are stored unchanged, including the agents' addresses and phone numbers on the candidate list.

sha256.meaning: SHA-256 of the bytes, which are in R2 under sha256/<first two characters>/<digest>. Every row that names a capture (capture_sha256, first_seen_capture, last_seen_capture) names this.

url.meaning: The URL the bytes were fetched from, after redirects, when first fetched.

content_type.meaning: The Content-Type the server sent, without parameters.

first_retrieved_at.meaning: When these bytes were first fetched.

last_retrieved_at.meaning: When these bytes were last fetched. A poll that finds the same bytes moves only this.

metadata.meaning: What the loader read from the capture about itself, such as published_at_as_shown (the candidate list's timestamp as printed).

elections/offices.note: One row per kind of seat, seeded from catalog/elections/<jurisdiction>.json and replaced on reload.

id.meaning: Path key of the office, such as ca/bc/legislative-assembly/mla.

title.meaning: The seat's title as the source shows it, such as Member of the Legislative Assembly.

title_fr.meaning: The French title, where the source gives one.
title_fr.blank_means: The source gives no French title.

body_name.meaning: The body the seat is on, such as Legislative Assembly of British Columbia.

body_level.meaning: The level of government of the body.

jurisdiction.meaning: Key of the jurisdiction in catalog/jurisdictions.json, a lowercase ISO 3166-2 code such as ca-bc.

source_url.meaning: The law or page that defines the office.

elections/elections.note: One row per election event run by one administrator on one schedule, seeded from the catalog. The deadlines and voting_notes are transcribed by hand from the captured voting information page (capture_sha256). Deadlines are ISO 8601 timestamps with offset, or dates.

id.meaning: Path key of the election, such as ca/bc/elections/2026-10-24-general.

jurisdiction.meaning: Key of the jurisdiction in catalog/jurisdictions.json, such as ca-bc.

administrator.meaning: The election authority, such as Elections BC.

called_on.meaning: The day the election was called.

return_day.meaning: The day the writs are returned.

registration_deadline_at.meaning: The last day to register in advance. In BC, to receive a Where to Vote card; voters can also register when they vote.
registration_deadline_at.blank_means: No such deadline, or not recorded.

mail_request_deadline_at.meaning: The last day or time to request a mail-in ballot.
mail_request_deadline_at.blank_means: No mail-in voting, or not recorded.

mail_return_deadline_at.meaning: When a mail-in ballot must be received.
mail_return_deadline_at.blank_means: No mail-in voting, or not recorded.

advance_voting_starts_at.meaning: The first opening of advance voting, in Pacific time for BC (voting_notes has the local hours).
advance_voting_starts_at.blank_means: No advance voting, or not recorded.

advance_voting_ends_at.meaning: The last close of advance voting.
advance_voting_ends_at.blank_means: No advance voting, or not recorded.

polls_open_at.meaning: When polls open on final voting day.

polls_close_at.meaning: When polls close on final voting day.

voting_notes.meaning: Everything else about how to vote, as the authority states it (eligibility, ID, where each method can be used, hours and time zones, other methods), in Markdown, one section per topic.

where_to_vote_url.meaning: The authority's page for finding a voting place. Voting places are not copied.

capture_sha256.meaning: The capture of the voting information page the deadlines and notes were taken from (elections/captures).
capture_sha256.blank_means: Not captured yet; the blocking check voting_info_captured fails.

elections/boundary_sets.note: One row per legal instrument or gazette that defines a set of districts or polling areas, seeded from the catalog.

id.meaning: Path key of the set, such as ca/bc/electoral-districts/2023 or ca/bc/voting-areas/2024-09-19.

jurisdiction.meaning: Key of the jurisdiction in catalog/jurisdictions.json.

kind.meaning: Which table the set's areas are in. district and whole_jurisdiction sets are in elections/districts; polling_area sets in elections/polling_areas.

kind_as_shown.meaning: The source's name for its areas, such as electoral district or voting area.

district_set_id.meaning: For a polling area set, the district set it subdivides.

legal_instrument.meaning: The law, order or gazette notice that defines the set, as named.
legal_instrument.blank_means: The set has none (a whole-jurisdiction set built from a cartographic file).

gazetted_on.meaning: The day the set was gazetted.

in_force_from.meaning: The first voting day the set governs.

in_force_to.meaning: The last voting day the set governs.

capture_sha256.meaning: The first page of the capture the set's areas were loaded from (elections/captures).

elections/districts.note: One row per area a contest is held in: an electoral district, ward or electoral area, or a whole jurisdiction for an at-large contest. BC's 93 electoral districts of 2023 come from the BC Geographic Warehouse (WHSE_ADMIN_BOUNDARIES.EBC_ELECTORAL_DISTS_BS11_SVW). Licence: Elections BC Open Data Licence.

boundary_set_id.meaning: The set the district belongs to (elections/boundary_sets).

code.meaning: The district's code as the source writes it, such as VPG. Unique within its set.

name_as_shown.meaning: The district's name as the source writes it, such as Vancouver-Point Grey.

geometry.meaning: The district's boundary. A source polygon that is invalid is repaired with ST_MakeValid on load; the original is in the capture. The blocking check geometry_valid tests every geometry.

elections/polling_areas.note: One row per area votes are counted in: a voting area, polling division or subdivision. BC's 5,778 voting areas gazetted 2024-09-19 (reused in 2026) come from the BC Geographic Warehouse (WHSE_ADMIN_BOUNDARIES.EBC_VOTING_AREAS_BS11_POLY_SVW). A voting area in several parts is one row. Licence: Elections BC Open Data Licence.

district_id.meaning: The district the area is in, in the set's district set. BC numbers voting areas within each district, so the code alone is not unique.

code.meaning: The area's code as shown, with any suffix, such as 042, 042A or 12-1.

parent_id.meaning: The polling area this one subdivides (a federal polling subdivision's division).
parent_id.blank_means: Not a subdivision (every BC voting area).

geometry.meaning: The area's boundary, repaired with ST_MakeValid when the source polygon is invalid (one 2024 BC voting area). The blocking check polling_areas_within_districts tests that each lies within its district, allowing 1% outside.

elections/contests.note: One row per race, one office in one district (or one referendum question), made from the catalog and the districts.

seats.meaning: How many are elected. 1 for an MLA.

method.meaning: The counting method. fptp is first past the post; block is multi-seat plurality; irv single-seat ranked; stv single transferable vote.

voting_day.meaning: The contest's voting day when it differs from the election's (a race restarted after a candidate's death).

question_text_fr.meaning: The French wording of a referendum question.
question_text_fr.blank_means: Not a referendum, or no French wording.

threshold_as_shown.meaning: What a referendum needs to pass, as the law words it.

elections/candidacies.note: One row per person's candidacy in one contest, as the latest capture shows it (current state; the history is in the captures). BC 2026: Elections BC's candidate list, which shows accepted nominations only; 2024: the names in the results. Names, agents' addresses and phone numbers are published as the source publishes them.

id.meaning: ULID of the candidacy, minted when first seen.

normalized_name.meaning: ballot_name casefolded, accents and punctuation stripped, spaces collapsed. Unique within a contest; a corrected spelling makes a new candidacy.

legal_name.meaning: The candidate's legal name, where published.

party_key.meaning: The party's key in the catalog's parties (such as bc-ndp), whose registered name is in party_names.
party_key.blank_means: Independent, no affiliation, or a label the catalog does not map yet (the check parties_mapped reports these).

party_as_shown.meaning: The affiliation as printed, such as BC NDP, Conservative Party, CWP or Independent.

status.meaning: The candidacy's status. A candidacy is on the current list when last_seen_capture is the latest list capture; one that drops off keeps its last status, since the list does not say why.

incumbent.meaning: Whether the source says the candidate holds the seat.

residence_address.meaning: The candidate's address (street and number), as the source publishes it.
residence_address.blank_means: Not published (BC's list publishes the agents' addresses, not the candidate's).

residence_province.meaning: The candidate's province, as a two-letter code.

residence_postal_code.meaning: The candidate's postal code, as published.

agents.meaning: The candidate's official and financial agents as the list publishes them, a list of {role (financial_agent or official_agent), name, address (the street lines, joined with ", "), city, province, postal_code, phone}. Since 2026-09-30 addresses and phone numbers are kept as published.
agents.blank_means: Empty list when the source names no agent (the 2024 results).
agents.known_gaps: An agent's field the source leaves blank is null; the BC list gives official agents no phone number.

first_seen_capture.meaning: The capture the candidacy was first seen in (elections/captures).

last_seen_capture.meaning: The latest capture that lists the candidacy.

status_changed_at.meaning: When we first saw the candidacy or its status change. An observation time, not when the change happened.
status_changed_at.blank_means: Never blank for rows loaded since 2026-09-30.

person_id.meaning: The person entity the candidate is, once a measured rule links candidacies to people.

note.meaning: Why a contact is proposed, rejected or stale.

platform.meaning: For a social account, its platform.
platform.blank_means: Empty string for every kind but social.

value.meaning: The contact, normalized: a phone number in E.164 (+16045550199), a lower-cased email, a website or donation URL as https://host/path without www., query or trailing slash, a social handle without @ (in/<name> on LinkedIn).

source_url.meaning: The page the value is on, as the agent cited it.

capture_sha256.meaning: The latest capture of source_url that verification or the recheck read (elections/captures).

linked_from_url.meaning: The trusted page that links to source_url (the party's page for the candidate, the legislature's, the election authority's).
linked_from_url.blank_means: source_url is itself trusted, or the agent gave none.

evidence_quote.meaning: The words next to the value on the page, as the agent quoted them (at most 500 characters). Not checked by code; the value is.

status.meaning: verified: code found the value on a fresh capture of source_url, near the candidate's surname (unless the page is on the candidate's verified website), and the page is trusted (Elections BC, the legislature, the candidate's party, the candidate's verified website) or a trusted page links to it near the name. proposed: not verified yet, or off a trusted chain, or the page could not be captured (note says which). rejected: the value is not on the page, not near the candidate's name, or is a party's own site. stale: a verified value the daily recheck no longer finds.
status.known_gaps: On a page that lists several candidates, near the surname is a weak test (1,500 characters); the 50-contact check before publication is the guard.

checked_at.meaning: When code last checked the value against a capture.

elections/contact_research.note: One row per candidacy the research agent was given under one pair (prompt, model, reasoning effort); a candidacy is never researched twice under the same pair. The run's budget and spend are its ai_spend row (mode contact_research).

pair_sha256.meaning: Digest of the pair (method, prompt, model, reasoning effort).

pair.meaning: The pair, as {method, prompt, model, reasoning_effort}.

state.meaning: answered (a valid answer, possibly with no contacts), refused, or failed (no valid answer).

rounds.meaning: Requests sent for the candidacy (at most 3).

pages.meaning: Every page the agent was shown, [{url, sha256}]; sha256 is blank for a page that could not be captured.

proposals.meaning: The contacts the agent proposed, as it returned them (kind, platform, value, source_url, linked_from_url, evidence_quote).

usage.meaning: Tokens used for the candidacy (input, cache, output, reasoning).

error.meaning: Why no valid answer came back.

elections/result_reports.note: One row per results response at one stage of counting; append-only. 2024: DataBC's results by voting place, as one official report. 2026: each changed Elections BC results page polled on election night and through the final count (elections/bc_results.py).

stage.meaning: The stage of counting: initial_count (election night, including partial updates), final_count (from the day Elections BC's page shows the final count in progress), judicial_recount, official (the Statement of Votes or equivalent).

polls_reported.meaning: Ballot boxes reported, summed over the districts, where the source gives "N of M" (the initial count).
polls_reported.blank_means: The source gives no such count (the final count's pages give a status per district instead).

polls_total.meaning: Ballot boxes in all, summed the same way.

published_at.meaning: When the source says the report is as of, in Pacific time with its offset. Elections BC labels it PST even in October; it is local time.
published_at.blank_means: The source gives no time (DataBC's CSV).

published_at_as_shown.meaning: The source's own words for published_at, such as "As of October 21, 2024 16:00 PST".

retrieved_at.meaning: When the response was fetched (its capture's last_retrieved_at when loaded).

capture_sha256.meaning: The capture the report was parsed from. Unique.

content_sha256.meaning: Digest of the report's stage and counts, without its time. A page republished with the same counts and a new "As of" adds no report.
content_sha256.blank_means: The 2024 official report (loaded before this column).

elections/results.note: Every count in a report, append-only; each report carries a full copy of the contests it covers. The latest counts of a contest are the rows of the latest report that covers it; counts at a stage the same within one stage. Unique on (report_id, contest_id, candidacy_id, answer, polling_area_id, unit_label_as_shown, ballot_type_as_shown, round, measure), nulls equal.

candidacy_id.meaning: The candidacy the votes are for.
candidacy_id.blank_means: A referendum answer or a contest-level measure.

answer.meaning: The referendum answer the votes are for, such as Yes.

measure.meaning: What value counts: votes; registered_electors; ballots_cast; rejected, declined and exhausted ballots; quota; other. Election-night pages add polls_reported and polls_total (ballot boxes reported, and in all, per district and ballot_type) and count_status (a status word the page shows instead of a number, in measure_as_shown, with value blank).

measure_as_shown.meaning: The source's name for the measure (Valid, Rejected, Total Valid Votes), or for count_status the status as shown (Complete, In Progress).

polling_area_id.blank_means: A district total, or a count reported by voting place or ballot type. Every BC row so far (2024 has no voting-area counts; election night is by district).

unit_label_as_shown.meaning: The source's own label for the counting unit, such as the voting place's name, or the election-night reporting row's label (Advance voting ballot boxes, Final Voting Day ballot boxes, Out-of-district ballots, Status).
unit_label_as_shown.blank_means: The count is for the whole contest.

ballot_type.meaning: How the ballots were cast, when the source splits by it.
ballot_type.blank_means: Not split by how ballots were cast.

ballot_type_as_shown.meaning: The source's category, such as Final voting, Advance voting - out-of-district or Vote by mail. Several map to one ballot_type.

value.blank_means: Withheld, not yet reported, counted in another unit (reported_under), or a count_status row. Never 0 for missing.

reported_under.meaning: For a unit the source combined into another for secrecy, that unit's label and ID; its own value is then blank.
